name: Divide By Zero
principle: The code uses a zero-capable value as the divisor in division or modulo. A zero denominator can raise an exception, signal, or crash and cause availability loss.
detection_signals: binary / operator with RHS variable or expression not proven nonzero
binary % operator with RHS variable or expression not proven nonzero
average/rate expression like total / count where count can be 0
dimension calculation like area / width, size / height, or scale / length where dimension comes from input
Java BigInteger.divide(x) or BigDecimal.divide(x) with x not checked against ZERO
C/C++ div(a,b), ldiv(a,b), lldiv(a,b), fmod(a,b), or remainder(a,b) with b not checked for 0
denominator computed from collection.size(), array.length, request count, width, height, or parsed numeric input without min > 0 validation
negative_signals: immediate guard before operation: if (denom == 0) throw/return and all paths stop
input validation enforces denom > 0 or denom < 0 before assignment/use
denominator is a literal nonzero constant
denominator is initialized to a nonzero constant and never reassigned before division
Java Objects.requireNonNull is not the only guard; code also checks compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) != 0 or signum() != 0
false_defense_traps: assert(denom != 0) or Java assert denom != 0; can be disabled in production
catching ArithmeticException but continuing with corrupt/default state
checking a value before conversion while the converted denominator can become 0, e.g. (int)smallDouble
validating only one branch while another division/modulo uses the same unchecked denominator
verification_focus: Can the RHS denominator of any /, %, divide, div, fmod, or remainder operation be zero on any reachable path?

consequence_chains.trigger: zero accepted from external input as count, size, width, height, or length
consequence_chains.consequence: crash, exit, restart, or unhandled exception causing DoS

consequence_chains.trigger: incorrect calculation derives a zero denominator

patch_principle: Validate every denominator immediately before division or modulo.
Reject or handle zero with throw, error return, or safe alternate computation.
Enforce positive minimums for counts, dimensions, sizes, and rates at input boundaries.
Test zero and empty-input cases with unit tests or fuzzing.

minimal_examples.safe: if (numRequests == 0) throw new ArithmeticException("divide by zero"); return totalTime / numRequests;
